#3346. Battlestar Galactica Franchise 2027 Return Officially Confirmed

Despite welcoming many reimaginings since it first premiered in 1978, Battlestar Galactica fans have been waiting a while to see what is next from the beloved sci-fi franchise.

After all, it was in 2010 that the prequel series, Caprica, premiered, and before that, the series that ran from 2004 to 2009 gave us a reimagining of the original television show. However, with a legion of fans still dedicated to the story which takes us to a group of planets known as the Twelve Colonies as we follow the exploits of the survivors who engage in an ongoing war with the Cylons, 2027 is the year when it is set to make a major return.

Unfortunately, back in 2024, Peacock broke fan's hearts when it announced that it would be scrapping its planned Battlestar Galactica reboot. Despite being in development for five years and announced back in 2019, the project, created by Mr. Robot's Sam Esmail, was rumored to follow the same vein as the 2004 reboot, but was reportedly canceled due to high production costs, creative friction, and a tighter streaming market.

However, it is not all bad news as Battlestar Galactica is expected to return in the new year thanks to one of the franchise's most beloved entries.

This is all courtesy of Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game as it is set to make an official comeback after almost two decades. Earlier this year, Ghost Galaxy revealed a new licensing agreement with Universal and Fantasy Flight Games and, as such, an updated edition of the beloved tabletop classic will begin a crowdfunding campaign in early 2027.

For those who missed out on its original iteration, Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game first launched in 2008 courtesy of Fantasy Flight Games. Created by Corey Konieczka, it swiftly became one of the most successful hidden-traitor games on the market, which makes it all the more exciting that it is set to return, and with a modern twist.

The original game is based on the 2004 reboot and will allow players to head to the Galactica in an attempt to secure humanity's dwindling resources, all whilst surviving Cylon attacks and various events which could see your ship damaged, or even destroyed. However, what made Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game all the more exciting is that it allowed some players to secretly be Cylons with the aim of sabotaging the other players.

The board game experience was so successful that it welcomed multiple expansions, including Pegasus, Exodus, and Daybreak, and even though it eventually stopped being created, secondhand copies of Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game soon became highly sought-after collectibles.

Whilst we do not yet know the specifics of the upcoming crowdfunding campaign, we do know that the updated Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game will feature an updated design, but what this will look like remains to be seen. Nevertheless, if you were a fan of the original experience, or just so happen to be a Battlestar Galactica fan who is eager for a return to the sci-fi world, make sure to keep up-to-date with this exciting new project.

From its birth in 2017 to a major redesign last year, we take an insider's look at the award-winning Helix Midnight Luxe and how it has cemented its position as one of the best luxury hybrids on the market

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It was 2013, and future Helix Sleep co-founders Adam Tishman, Jerry Lin and Kristian von Rickenbach had a simple mission: to find a comfy new mattress that wouldn't break the bank.

But instead of an enjoyable shopping experience, the trio were faced with confusing online cliches, or pricey mattresses from brick and mortar stores.

Quickly, an opportunity sprung up in front of them: to disrupt a tired industry and subsequently create one of America's leading sleep brands.

Fast forward to present day and Helix Sleep is making some of the best mattresses we've tested, chief among them being the Helix Midnight Luxe, which is currently 25% off at Helix.

In an exclusive interview for Tom's Guide, Helix co-founder Jerry Lin talks us through the conception, creation and rebirth of the Midnight Luxe, our top-rated mattress for side sleepers, and what the future looks like for this award-wining bed.

The Midnight Luxe is always included in the monthly Helix mattress sale, but this month's discount is higher than normal. For Black Friday you can save 25% on every size, with a queen costing $1,874 (was $2,498). You'll also get a year's sleep trial, lifetime warranty, and free shipping.

Tishman, Lin and von Rickenbach identified three big problems when trying to buy a new mattress:

The trio started working with sleep PHD researchers in Europe to design a line of mattresses that weren't one-size-fits-all, but instead distinguishable by sleep position. (And by looking closely at our sleep DNA, the brand name Helix was born.)

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

When Helix Sleep finally launched in 2015, they did so with a direct-to-consumer model. They sought to demystify the mattress buying process by creating bespoke mattresses based on your answers to the Helix Sleep quiz.

After thousands of online orders, in 2017 the brand mined the sleep quiz data to roll out a basic range of mattresses that catered to every major sleep position.

Soon after, the original Helix Midnight entered the online marketplace. Now the entry level bed in the brand's expanded range, the Core Midnight is designed to meet the needs of a typical side sleeper; cushioning at the shoulders, hips and knees, and support at the lower back.

In terms of mattress firmness, we'd rate the Core Midnight as a medium. It was a great start for improved side sleep comfort, but the best was yet to come...

In 2018, Helix Sleep launched the Luxe Collection. Maintaining its philosophy of mattresses tailored for every individual sleep need, this new and more luxurious range of beds aimed to elevate the comfort of the Core mattresses to appeal to customers seeking a truly indulgent sleep.

The original inspiration was straightforward: take the medium-feel of our original Helix Midnight and elevate it with the comfort, materials, and craftsmanship you'd expect from a luxury hotel mattress

“The Helix Luxe Collection is our most popular mattress line, with the Midnight Luxe consistently ranking as our best-selling model,” reveals Lin, a Wharton MBA who began his career in investment banking.

“The original inspiration was straightforward: take the medium-feel, side-sleeper-friendly design of our original Helix Midnight and elevate it with the comfort, materials, and craftsmanship you'd expect from a luxury hotel mattress, but at a much more accessible price point."

The timing of the 2018 launch couldn’t have been better. With original mattress-in-a-box brands Casper and Purple disrupting the traditional brick-and-mortar mattress industry, Helix and its Luxe line became an integral part of the growing boxed bed revolution.

Then, just two years later, many parts of the States found themselves under stay-at-home orders as part of Covid-19 quarantine measures.

One of Helix's biggest competitive advantages is that we manufacture our own foam

With 'work from bed' the new normal for many Americans, and with little else to spend hard-earned cash on, the e-commerce mattress industry boomed.

Some even reported that the Helix Midnight Luxe was the only thing helping them sleep during those uncertain times.

With the bed-to-door industry on fast forward, Helix wanted to keep the Midnight Luxe ahead of the curve. The answer lay in doubling down: improving the mattress from base to quilted cover.

The Midnight Luxe stands at 13.5" tall and is crafted from a combination of coils and comfort foam.

Each layer serves a specific purpose for its overall sleep comfort.

From top to bottom, let's take a closer look at the Luxe's overall structure:

A soft, breathable cover sits above two layers of premium quilting foam (1.5 lb and gel-infused 1.8 lb), creating a plush sleep surface that's both comfortable and durable. The standard cover is made with TENCEL fabric.

An additional layer of gel memory foam provides targeted pressure relief, particularly around the shoulders and hips, making the Midnight Luxe especially well-suited for side sleepers. This gel memory foam has an IFD (Indentation Force Deflection) of 10-18 and a density of 1.8-4.0 PCF.

Helix's signature titanium, graphite, and copper infused memory foam delivers deeper contouring and is engineered for temperature management and long-term durability. It has a 4lb foam density, which is more than double the 2lb density of many foams used by standard brands.

Next, A firmer transition layer, with lower density foam, creates a gradual shift from the plush comfort layers to the supportive coil system underneath. This helps prevent the sensation of sinking too deeply into the mattress.

Up to 1,000 individually wrapped eight-inch coils provide responsive support, with enhanced reinforcement in the lumbar region to help promote healthy spinal alignment. Reinforced perimeter coils also improve edge support, making the full surface of the mattress more usable. Each coil is made from tempered steel and wrapped in polypropylene non-woven fabric.

The Helix Midnight Luxe is a luxury hybrid mattress. While the coils are in important factor in the bed's overall comfort layer, it is the proprietary foams that help set this boxed bed apart from many competitors.

While most brands use pre-poured foams from third party suppliers, Helix manufacture their own foam (more on this below). This should allow them to fine tune its construction until the optimal level of comfort is achieved. A feat I think they've pulled it off.

As someone who sleeps predominantly on my side and occasionally on my back, I feel as though the Helix Midnight Luxe has been crafted specifically for me in way that I haven't experienced while testing another mattress

The foams provide just the right amount of body-contouring support across the shoulders, hips and knees, while holding the spine in healthy alignment with the rest of the body.

In 2022, Helix merged with sleep brand Brooklyn Bedding. Now operating from its own factory in Arizona, Helix began experimenting with pouring and manufacturing its own mattress foam, alongside its own coils.

This decision proved to be a pivotal moment in the development of the Midnight Luxe.

“One of Helix's biggest competitive advantages is something most consumers never see: we manufacture our own foam,” explains Lin, who built the finance and operations backbone behind Helix’s growth and helps steer the brand’s product innovation and retail expansion.

“Many mattress brands are essentially assemblers. They source foam, coils, and other components from third-party suppliers and combine them into a finished product.

“At Helix, we take a different approach. We manufacture our core components ourselves, giving us significantly more control over material quality, performance, and cost.

“A perfect example is the proprietary memory foam we developed specifically for the Luxe Collection.”

We developed a high-density, 4lb memory foam infused with titanium, graphite and copper

“For the latest Midnight Luxe, we developed a high-density, 4lb memory foam infused with titanium, graphite and copper,” explains Lin. “This is one of the most important innovations in the redesigned mattress.”

Foam density is an important factor in overall durability. Higher-density memory foams can offer greater resistance to daily use, wear and compression, helping the Midnight Luxe to maintain its comfort and support through years of use.

And with a queen costing in the region of $1,900 when not on sale, durability is crucial.

However, as someone who has tested both versions of the Helix Midnight Luxe, it's worth noting that the trade off of this durability is that the 2025 redesigned model is slightly firmer.

"At 4lb per cubic foot, this is a premium-density memory foam engineered for long-term performance," explains Lin.

For context, many luxury manufacturer's use foams under 2lb in density, with 1.8lb considered an acceptable density.

Helix also incorporates three distinct materials into the foam formulation, each selected for its specialist properties. These are:

By manufacturing its own foam, the brand can refine density, responsiveness and body-cradling characteristics until it's achieved the desired balance.

For the Midnight Luxe in particular, that means "deep pressure relief without sacrificing the support that makes the [mattress] so comfortable," says Lin.

"It's a level of material customization that would be much more difficult if we were simply purchasing off-the-shelf foam."

“While the deeper comfort layers are important, we also paid attention to the part of the mattress you feel first: the quilted pillow top,” says Lin.

"The plush pillow top is a quilted comfort system made with two layers of high-density foam, a 1.5lb layer and a 1.8lb gel-infused layer.

“These layers are designed to provide immediate cushioning and pressure relief, particularly around sensitive areas like the shoulders and hips."

While pressure relief is a crucial feature of any mattress designed specifically for side sleepers, there was another reason the brand invested in higher-density materials at the top — durability.

"The uppermost layers of a mattress experience significant daily compression and wear," explains Lin. "Using higher-quality foam in these layers helps the Midnight Luxe to maintain its comfort characteristics over time.

"By incorporating 1.5lb and 1.8lb foams, we're making a deliberate investment in materials that go beyond what's commonly used in the industry."

For context, both the Saatva Classic, the highest-scoring mattress we've ever tested, and the DreamCloud Classic, our second highest ranking mattress overall because of its superb value for money, use a foam density of 1.4lb in their Euro top covers, which are inherently different by design to the plush pillow top on the Midnight Luxe.

The Helix Midnight Luxe launched in 2018 as a luxury hotel-style upgrade to the original Midnight (now marketed as the Core Midnight). It has a plush pillow top and zoned lumbar support for back pain relief.

"Those features helped establish the Luxe Collection as our most popular mattress line," says Lin.

"But as our manufacturing capabilities evolved, we saw an opportunity to make more meaningful improvements to the mattress itself."

In 2025, Helix introduced the most significant redesign of the Luxe Collection since its launch.

Rather than focusing on cosmetic changes or additional features, they sought to reengineer the mattress from the inside out.

"These improvements reflect how we think about product development at Helix," says Lin.

"We're constantly looking for ways to improve the actual sleep experience, whether that's through better pressure relief, more consistent support, improved temperature regulation, or materials that maintain their performance longer.

"Ultimately, our philosophy is simple: a luxury mattress should be defined by the quality of what's inside it, not just how it looks or how much it costs," concludes Lin.

"That's what guided the latest Midnight Luxe redesign, and it's what continues to drive our approach to mattress innovation."

Of course, the pair have since been reunited and even made the jump to the big screen together, and just in time for Christmas, there's a rather lovely way for younger Star Wars fans to revisit their adventures, as long as nobody eats some frog alien eggs.

Lucasfilm's The Mandalorian Adventures with Grogu Pop-Up Storybook is officially available now. The book comes from Matthew Reinhart, whose work as a paper engineer has seen him bring everything from Hogwarts to the worlds of Disney and Star Wars to life in three dimensions. The book takes readers through all three seasons of The Mandalorian, from the moment Din first laid eyes on the little creature he'd been paid to retrieve to Grogu's decision to abandon his Jedi training and return to the man who'd effectively become his father. #3342. Prime Video’s New 8-Part Sci-Fi Thriller Delivers A Masterclass In Cyberpunk Worldbuilding

Prime Video's new 8-part sci-fi thriller delivers a masterclass in cyberpunk worldbuilding, bringing an iconic, breathtaking dystopian future to life. Released in full on Wednesday, November 25, this brand new series is one of the best new binges on Prime Video this weekend and is expected to be one of the most-watched shows across all streaming platforms in the coming days. With its striking visual style and rich production design based on a brilliant sci-fi franchise, there is no better new series to watch right now with remarkable worldbuilding.

Blade Runner 2099 just arrived with all 8 episodes on Prime Video this Wednesday, November 25. While early reviews are mostly, but not unanimously, positive, earning a Rotten Tomatoes score of 68%, the series' greatest achievement is its rich setting that evolves the original dystopian cyberpunk feel and lore from the original Blade Runner film. Set 50 years after the events of Blade Runner 2049, which is widely considered one of the top sci-fi sequels ever made, Blade Runner 2099 delivers a masterclass in expanding a beloved classic story world.

While both Blade Runner and Blade Runner 2049 established a legendary dystopian world that presents a not-so-distant Los Angeles full of tall skyscrapers, neon lights, and a perpetually unsettling atmosphere, Blade Runner 2099 takes these elements one step further by placing the megacity under Replicant control. After humankind lost a major war to the Replicants, the city's framework and power dynamics have fundamentally changed, adding a fascinating new thematic layer to the already ominous dystopian landscape. This also takes the initial cyberpunk design of the franchise's LA setting one step further, leaning more heavily into urban decay contrasted by advanced tech.

With Replicants in control of Los Angeles in Blade Runner 2099, humans have devolved into being second-class citizens, and the distinct visual style of LA has also undergone massive changes to align with this extreme power shift. Unlike the Blade Runner films, 2099 features a new signature aesthetic, replacing the dark and rainy weather system with oppressive light and heat, which completely alters the visual identity of the franchise. The 50-year time jump between 2049 and 2099 also introduces new societal customs and technological abilities that demonstrate the Replicants' rise to power, adding even more worldbuilding elements to an already well-established sci-fi universe.

Apart from the Replicants taking over Los Angeles in Prime Video's new Blade Runner series, the most revolutionary change in 2099 is how the series views oppression, power, and justice, which builds on the franchise's legacy of dystopian storytelling. Rather than having humans continue to determine the quality of life over Replicants, the Replicants now wield the authority to categorize humans, which is a direct reversal of the pre-existing core theme in the previous two Blade Runner installments.

All 62 episodes of Prime Video's acclaimed sci-fi masterpiece deliver gripping interplanetary warfare, extraordinary characters, & epic storytelling.

2099 could have easily maintained this essential factor in the new Prime Video series, but flipping its core moral question on its head is a testament to the franchise's willingness to broaden its own horizons while still holding firmly to its dystopian roots. Hunter Schafer's Cora, a human protagonist and fugitive, experiences similar forms of oppression and social discrimination that Replicants had suffered for multiple decades, while Michelle Yeoh's Replicant character, Olwen, confronts her own conflict with mortality and her life's value as an AI entity.

Although not all critics have praised Blade Runner 2099 as a whole, most contend that the worldbuilding and franchise expansion are some of its strongest and most appealing qualities. IndieWire writes, "Blade Runner 2099 may not be as exquisite as its predecessors (and it won’t likely win over audiences who aren’t already fans), but it nails the franchise’s aura — and builds one awesome world." Additionally, Empire Magazine notes, "It may sometimes lose narrative momentum but this is world-building par excellence, high on atmosphere, spectacle and food for thought." Ultimately, Blade Runner 2099 may be flawed, but it's a masterclass in crafting an immersive sci-fi world.

#3339. Why Black Friday Is the Perfect Time to Start a Gym Membership

Most people are probably waiting until Jan. 1 to start getting in shape, whether they want to start fresh or absolve themselves of their perceived holiday indulgences. Every year, people start the new year by joining a gym crowded with others newly resolved to get in shape, paying full price for the privilege of waiting in a long line to use the squat rack. This year, try something different: Start your gym membership during Black Friday.

The week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit. While you're comparing deals on new tech, headphones, or smart home devices, here’s why you should also take a few minutes to scout out the gyms near you.

This week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a new air fryer. Here are just a few examples of the offers out there right now:

Anytime Fitness is running a Black Friday offer for new members who sign up between Nov. 20 and Nov. 30, 2026, with monthly fees waived for the rest of the year in the promotion's terms (the standard access fee still applies, and terms vary by country and club, so confirm with your local location).

Orangetheory and F45 have various free-month and prize-entry promotions for new Black Friday sign-ups, and similar studios for Pilates, yoga, and strength training have discounted multi-month and annual packages.

Independent gyms, university rec centers, and local studios often run their own versions, from a free month tacked onto a longer commitment to waived joining fees.

Deals vary a lot by location, so call or stop by the clubs near you and ask what's available. Then remember to always read the fine print before you sign:

Look at the price after the promotion ends, not just the first month's rate.

Ask about fees, including joining, annual, and access fees.

Try before you buy. Many gyms offer a free trial pass. It might make sense to first visit at the time of day you'd actually go.

Be honest about distance. The best gym is the one you'll actually walk into, so pick one that's close to home or work.

Gyms also run sales around New Year's, so a good Black Friday offer isn't the only deal you'll see. Even still, the savings aren't the only reason to go now.

December is reliably the quietest stretch of the gym year: People are busy with holiday travel and work deadlines, and many tell themselves they'll "start fresh in January." That means open benches, free treadmills, and staff who have time to show you how a machine works.

That's a gift for any gym-goer, but especially if you're new. Learning your way around a gym is much less intimidating when it's empty. You can figure out the equipment, make your mistakes in peace, and build a routine before the January crowds arrive. Plus, this time of year is a perfect window to set and achieve a winnable goal.

From Black Friday to New Year's Day is about five weeks. By the time the January rush hits its peak and settles into its usual patterns, you could be eight weeks into a new routine. And as my colleague Beth Skwarecki explains, you really can get a lot stronger in 24 workouts. Beginners tend to see the fastest gains of their lifting lives in the first couple of months.

Prefer running? I know I do, and luckily, a couch-to-5K plan works the same way. Most programs run about nine weeks and build you up gradually from short run-walk intervals. Start the week after Black Friday and you'll be running for a solid stretch by early January, and you'll be well on your way to 30 minutes at a stretch by the end of the month. By the time your New Year's resolution friends are just starting, you'll already be a few runs in.

This is also the season when many workplaces and health plans wrap up their open enrollment periods, which makes it a smart time to check what wellness perks you already have. Before you pay full price for anything, look into:

Workplace wellness programs, which sometimes offer gym reimbursements, discounted memberships or fitness stipends.

Health insurance perks, since some plans include gym memberships or discounts.

HSA and FSA rules, where general gym memberships usually don't qualify, but some medically recommended programs may. Also check any year-end deadlines for money you'd otherwise lose.

Corporate and employer discounts, which many large gyms offer on top of regular promotions.

Stack a workplace benefit on top of a holiday sale, and your cost per workout can drop considerably—well before New Year's resolution time arrives.

#3335. iOS 27 has clever new Messages feature I’ve been using a lot

iOS 27 gives the Messages app a variety of welcome upgrades, including one I’ve found myself using a lot: a Smart Reply feature that’s now personalized to the user’s writing style.

When the first wave of Apple Intelligence features were announced in 2024, one that I immediately thought sounded useful was Smart Reply.

The idea behind Smart Reply is simple. Rather than needing to manually type out replies in Messages and Mail, your iPhone can offer prewritten replies you can choose and send with a couple taps.

Great in theory, but the ‘Smart’ part of Smart Reply struggled to materialize in iOS 18.

Fortunately, with a key Apple Intelligence upgrade in iOS 27, the new version of the feature finally lives up to its name. Per Apple:

Smart Reply in Mail and Messages can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.

Before, Smart Reply would look at the context of a conversation to craft its suggestions. But now, it also aims to match your writing style, punctuation, and tone.

In iOS 18, I almost never used Smart Reply. That’s because despite being fine at suggesting replies that technically worked, those suggestions didn’t sound like me at all.

That’s changed in iOS 27. Smart Reply now consistently impresses me. It no longer offers generic responses that sound like AI wrote them. Instead, its suggestions actually fit with my normal style of communication.

The only drawback is that right now, you’ll only ever see two Smart Reply suggestions. If Apple expanded the feature by letting you scroll horizontally through more options, I suspect I’d use Smart Reply even more.

Each season builds longing through classic romance setups, from fake dating to enemies-to-lovers narratives, that make the payoff feel earned. With strict Regency social rules in mind, Bridgerton leads with reality, employing brilliant intimacy coordinators to choreograph the moments that emphasize emotional connection, consent, and the female gaze. Perhaps the only downside to these steamy scenes is the expectations they establish in our world! Damn you, Simon Basset (Regé-Jean Page)!

Four Netflix characters, four completely different ways of showing up for somebody. This is the one who fits how you actually do friendship, and what having them in your life would be like.

You do not do friendship at half volume, and neither does he. What you want is somebody who says yes to the plan before you have finished describing the plan.

You are the friend who makes things happen, and so is she. Together you would be mildly exhausting to everyone around you and completely delighted with yourselves.

You have no patience for pleasant lies, and she has no ability to tell them. What looks like coldness from the outside is the most reliable friendship on this list.

You look after whoever is having the worst day. So does he. It is the least strategic way to move through the world and the best possible quality in a friend.

Perhaps one of the most important queer stories ever told, Fellow Travelers, based on the Thomas Mallon novel, is an emotionally charged, decades-spanning romance. The romantic thriller chronicles the secret love affair between two very different men, State Department official Hawkins Fuller (Matt Bomer) and idealistic congressional staffer Tim Laughlin (Jonathan Bailey), who meet in 1950s Washington, D.C. Beginning at the height of the McCarthy-era Lavender Scare in which the government actively hunted down and purged gay employees, Hawkins and Tim's clandestine relationship is tested by political paranoia, personal betrayal, and societal bigotry. With sweeping historical scope, Fellow Travelers preserves a crucial moment in history through explicit, frank intimacy driven by repressed desire, shifting power dynamics, and high-stakes historical danger.

Created by Ron Nyswaner, Fellow Travelers is a brilliant character-driven drama. The series does a stand-up job at presenting fully-fleshed individuals who must balance their personal desires with a fight to survive. These characters must guard every word and gesture in public. But then, behind closed doors, physical passion acts as an urgent release, heightening the power of intimacy. These moments range from tenderness, roughness, control, and surrender. As out actors, Bomer and Bailey have remarkable chemistry, understanding the gravity of these moments between Hawkins and Tim. While some scenes may be graphic, they're balanced with truth. These scenes will certainly make you blush, but they'll also hit your heart hard.

We're going to the cottage! Very few shows took the world by storm quite like Heated Rivalry. Created by Jacob Tierney and based on Rachel Reid's Game Changers book series, the Canadian romance series follows rival hockey superstars, Shane Hollander (Hudson Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Connor Storrie). Over an eight-year span, the opposing captains engage in a secret, passionate romantic relationship off the ice while maintaining a fierce public rivalry on it. Together, they navigate intense professional pressures, family expectations, and the personal risks of keeping their love hidden in the high-stakes world of professional sports. Heated Rivalry examines toxic masculinity and the pressures of staying closeted in athletics while celebrating themes of identity, queer joy, and acceptance.

Heated Rivalry emerged as a breakout hit because it immediately dove deep into the intimacy. It pairs explicit, consent-driven romance with high-stakes tension and emotional vulnerability. Physical encounters act as an early language between Shane and Ilya while they struggle with verbal honesty and public expectations. As their bond shifts over time, so does their ability to communicate their true feelings. The scenes, staged by intimacy coordinator Chala Hunter, feel lived-in, playful, and emotionally grounded, balancing humor, awkwardness, and tenderness. Rather than lean into tragic tropes where intimacy leads to ruin, the narrative highlights the impact of true love, mutual respect, and emotional payoff. Beyond Shane and Ilya, Heated Rivalry crafts their own rivalry as the beautiful relationship between Scott Hunter (François Arnaud) and Kip Grady (Robbie G.K.) showcases a very different connection. Heated Rivalry became an instant obsession because the love is real. Come for the smut, stay for the love!

Based on the book series by Diana Gabaldon, the historical fantasy series Outlander is quite a compelling story. Developed by Ronald D. Moore, Outlander follows Claire Randall (Caitríona Balfe), a British World War II combat nurse who is mysteriously swept back in time from 1945 to 1743 Scotland. Forced to marry a chivalrous Highland warrior named Jamie Fraser (Sam Heughan) for protection, she falls deeply in love with him as she navigates a dangerous world. Torn between two eras and two men, Claire uses her modern medical skills to survive as she and Jamie become entangled in major historical upheavals, from the Jacobite Rising to the American Revolution. Outlander blends a time-travel mystery, historical drama, and an intense romance rooted in high-stakes survival with rich period pieces.

Outlander appealed to viewers looking for multi-genre drama handled with care. The eight-season series flourishes with its emotional depth and steamy romance, but it also does feature significant graphic violence, explicit torture, and sexual assault scenes. That said, those moments are counterbalanced by its intimacy. It focuses on desire and partnership. Claire openly initiates and enjoys sexual moments, while Jamie's devotion and low ego put his partner's feelings first. As Jamie and Claire grow older and face major trials and tribulations, the intimacy shifts from early, urgent passion to deeper trust and emotional understanding. With time travel, clan politics, and a lush Scottish locale setting the scene, Outlander masters heightened intimate tension in every moment the pair get together.

Inspired by 44 Chapters About 4 Men by BB Easton, the two-season erotic drama Sex/Life follows Billie Connelly (Sarah Shahi), a suburban wife and mother of two, who feels unfulfilled by the fading passion in her stable marriage to her husband, Cooper (Mike Vogel). Torn between her domestic life and memories of her wild past in New York City, Billie begins documenting her explicit fantasies about her bad-boy ex-boyfriend, Brad Simon (Adam Demos), in a private journey. When Cooper discovers the diary and Brad re-enters her life, Billie's past and present collide in a complicated love triangle. Sex/Life is a perfect series for those who love high-stakes melodrama, intense chemistry, and bold explorations of desire, identity, and marital complacency.

Sex/Life leads with a bold and provocative tone. With frequent nudity, candid conversations about desire, and steamy scenes until your heart's content, Sex/Life leans heavily into the crossroads of adult romance and soap opera intrigue. Beyond the fantasy elements, the series touches on losing the spark in long-term partnerships and balancing personal desires with necessary responsibilities. Created by Stacy Rukeyser, the show uses sex scenes to reflect shifting dynamics with Billie's "85/15" relationship tension, tapping into the friction between security and wilder impulses. At only 14 episodes, Sex/Life is a highly addictive, bingeable drama.

No show is as addictively frustrating as Tell Me Lies. Created by Meaghan Oppenheimer and based on the Carola Lovering novel, the three-season series follows the tumultuous, eight-year relationship between Lucy Albright (Grace Van Patten) and Stephen DeMarco (Jackson White) after they meet at Baird College. What starts as a typical campus romance quickly spirals into addiction, deceit, and emotional dependency. Jumping between their college years and the 2015 wedding of their friends Bree (Catherine Missal) and Evan (Brandon Cook), Tell Me Lies explores how Lucy and Stephen's destructive bond and dark secrets permanently alter the lives of everyone in their friend group. Tell Me Lies is a character-driven drama that leans heavily into the honest, messy relationships based on toxic pairings and psychological manipulation where sex is front and center.

While Tell Me Lies is filled to the brim with campus drama and steamy scenes, it's rooted in real emotional vulnerabilities. The show looks beyond surface-level romance to examine why people surrender their truth and self-respect to belong. The sexual scenes are presented as purpose-driven storytelling moments. Intimate scenes often highlight power shifts, emotional dependency, or shifting relationship dynamics rather than serving purely as filler fodder. Rather than reducing characters to simple heroes or villains, Tell Me Lies tackles insecurity, avoidance, and how small choices reshape an individual's personality and identity. The action escalates across each season, culminating in a shockingly obvious conclusion. If there’s one thing to take away from Tell Me Lies, it’s this: do not be like these people. None of them. They may have a redeemable quality or two, but they all display moments of manipulation that drop them into dangerous territory.

At the forefront of the early 2000s vampire obsession, True Blood was one of HBO's early smut spectacles of its heyday. The fantasy horror drama from Alan Ball follows Sookie Stackhouse (Anna Paquin), a telepathic waitress in the small town of Bon Temps, Louisiana, in a world where the invention of synthetic blood allows vampires to coexist publicly with humans. When Sookie falls in love with a mysterious 174-year-old vampire named Bill Compton (Stephen Moyer), her quiet life is upended as she is pulled into a dangerous underworld of vampire politics, werewolves, witches, and fairies. Blending dark romance, mystery, and Southern Gothic horror, True Blood explores the violent social clashes between humans and supernatural beings over assimilation and equal rights. Based on Charlaine Harris' The Southern Vampire Mysteries, True Blood balances pulpy escapism with masterful worldbuilding and distinct character development.

True Blood is the perfect balance of camp, romance, and grit. It shifts between murder mysteries, romantic entanglements, heavy gore, and self-aware humor without treating its melodrama as a distraction. True Blood leans into unapologetic sensuality, where desire is central to the plot. Vampire blood acts as both sustenance and an intoxicating, sensory trigger that blurs pain, pleasure, and power. It's the rush of intimate ecstasy that turns romance into a thrill ride. The story uses its setting's heat, humidity, and secrets to heighten the tension. At the same time, the concept of the "vampires out of the coffin" premise serves as a sharp debate on social and queer themes. From Sookie and Eric Northman's (Alexander Skarsgård) rival-to-romance tension-filled chemistry to Jason Stackhouse (Ryan Kwanten) and Jessica Hamby's (Deborah Ann Woll) chaotic, impulsive hookups, True Blood is never short of sex and intimacy. Even supernatural dream sequences are sexy spectacles! True Blood is not a show to watch with your parents around, no matter your age!

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#3331. HomeKit Weekly: Lafaer’s 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes an annoying automation in Apple Home

Motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home. The only carve-out is lighting, because some rooms are hard to judge by time of day alone. Depending on the windows and placement against the sun, some rooms might need light-based automations earlier in the day than others. The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes that with a light sensor most motion sensors lack, along with mmWave radar.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations. If you’re still for long periods, you’re invisible, and the automation assumes the room is empty. The Lafaer LWR02 pairs PIR with 2.4 GHz mmWave radar. The PIR-based motion sees you walking in, and the radar sees the minor stuff, like breathing and shifting on the couch, so the room stays “occupied” for as long as you are in it. The two together also reduce false positives from ceiling fans, curtains, and the dog, because the radar and PIR both must agree before the sensor reports motion.

In Apple Home, that shows up as an occupancy sensor and a motion sensor from the same device.

“Turn on the lights when someone enters” is a common automation I use, but it can be tricky. What if you only want it when it’s not light outside? Doing it based on time of day sometimes works, but what about depending on where the windows are facing, etc.? You might have a room that gets darker an hour earlier than another room. “Turn on the lights when someone enters, and it’s dark in the room” is what the light sensor can handle for you.

In the Home app, that means triggering a sensor for occupancy, then converting the automation into a Shortcut and adding a condition for the light level. It’s a few extra steps, but it does really give you more fine control over how it works.

Presence, motion, light, temperature, and humidity all come from the same device, and each one appears in Apple Home as its own sensor, so you can build automations around whichever ones fit the room.

It’s IPX3-rated, so bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry rooms are fine to use in. Coverage is about 13 feet for presence and 26 for motion across about 120 degrees, which works in a bedroom, office, or bathroom. It’s not going to cover a great room from one corner. The base is a magnetic half sphere, so you can aim it, and it mounts with adhesive or sits on a shelf. I generally like to use the shelf for these types of sensors.

The Lafaer LWR02 is Matter over Thread, so it pairs directly with a HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K with no Lafaer hub or account needed. It runs on two included AAA batteries, is rated for up to two years, and rechargeable AAAs work with it as well. Thread is why a sensor doing this much can last that long on batteries. All sensor data is processed locally, so it only uses a trickle on the batteries.

Lights that turn off while you’re sitting still in the room are the reason a lot of people stop using motion automations in smart homes. The Lafaer LWR02 fixes that with mmWave radar and then lets you have more granular control of light-based automations based on what’s actually in the environment in the room, not just the time of day.

The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor is available on Amazon.

#3330. 12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

This series will help you pick the perfect presents, decor, and activities to make this Christmas the Best Christmas Ever.

In a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it. You get to enjoy all the brightly colored lights your neighbors put up, but you don’t have to put up your own. You don’t have to do any duty-shopping. There's no pressure. But Christmas Day itself leaves you in a mostly shuttered world that feels like there’s nothing going on. Fortunately, there are options to make Dec. 25 a fun day off, regardless of your observances.

You can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex. Chinese restaurants and movie theaters traditionally stay open on Christmas Day for those who don't celebrate, and they’re often filled with fellow Christmas refugees. Check Google for the hours of your local Chinese restaurant and give them a call to make a reservation. If you’re more adventurous and you’re in a city large enough to have a Chinatown (or a whatever-town), just head straight there on Christmas and see what happens—that’s how the best days usually start.

If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses. Just make sure you check first. Lots of chain restaurants are open on Christmas Day too, including Applebee's, McDonald’s, Benihana, and more. You can even get Christmas breakfast at your local IHOP. But not every location of every outlet follows the same hours.

As for movies, most chain multiplex theaters are open on Dec. 25, and theaters are usually pretty full. The movies attract both people who don't celebrate Christmas and people who do, but want to get away from their families for a couple hours, so make sure and reserve a seat beforehand. Consider hitting up an out-of-the-way spot or that theater with the table service and cushy recliners to make it feel like more of an occasion.

Most people going to the movies on Christmas Day aren’t there for Christmas movies, so interesting “secular” movies are often slated for release on the 25th. This year's Christmas is unusually packed with interesting new movies, including family flick Jumani: Open World, a Robert Eggers horror movie called Werwulf, and the crowd pleasing football story Mr. Irrelevant, so you have serious options.

Chinese restaurants and movie theaters aren’t the only establishments open on Christmas. Here are some other options:

Go skiing or snowboarding: Most mountains are open on Christmas, and the lift lines are blissfully empty. There's no better way of celebrating a winter-based holiday than on a wide-open mountain.

Visit a skating rink: Speaking of winter sports, ice skating rinks are generally open on Christmas too.

Pretend to be a tourist: Tourist attractions are often open on Christmas, especially in larger cities. This includes places like Madame Tussaud’s and Ripley’s Believe It or Not, as well as ziplines and Segway tours—so do that touristy thing you’ve never done before.

Get a room: If you’ve got some spare cash and have nothing better to do, get a room at a hotel. Hotels don’t usually close on Christmas, and they typically offer plenty of amenities, so take advantage of the pool at the Holiday Inn or the spa at the Four Seasons, depending on your lifestyle.

Hiking and biking: Hiking trails and parks are open on Christmas if you want to get outdoors. If you’re into biking, hit the trails or hit the streets: Traffic is minimal on Christmas, so it’s a great time to put in some serious roadwork.

Volunteer: Not having anything to do on Christmas isn’t the biggest life problem, especially compared to people who have nowhere to go and nothing to eat. So use Christmas to help people and actually deliver on that whole “good will towards men” thing. Check your local Craigslist for volunteering opportunities.

Use Christmas as a catch-up day: This is strictly for type-A people, but if everyone is out of town and no one is going to call you, why not spend the day catching up on neglected chores or personal projects? You can spend at least part of your day knocking a few things off your to-do list and the rest of the time relaxing. That way you’ll get a break and still feel accomplished.

Just sleep all day: Type-B personalities like me see a day free of obligations and other people as a golden opportunity to do as little as is humanly possible, a day to fully commit to sloth.

Spend time with friends and family at home: Not celebrating Christmas doesn’t mean you can’t spend the day with family and/or friends. Get together with your loved ones, play games, watch a movie, cook together, talk, or whatever else you all enjoy. You don’t have to go out to have fun, so don’t rule out staying in with people you care about.

Shopping: This is at the bottom of the list because it’s iffy. Drug stores and convenience stores like 711 are usually open on the 25th. Grocery chains like Kroger’s and Trader Joe’s usually aren’t. Your local shopping mall or retail district might be open, but probably won't be, so check ahead.

Because so many places are closed on Christmas Day, you should plan ahead (unless you like spontaneity and are OK with the possibility of disappointment) by:

Making a list of the places you want to go.

Calling nearby locations to confirm they’ll be open, as not every chain follows corporate holiday hour recommendations.

Making reservations at any restaurant(s) you plan to visit.

Putting together a basic timeline of the day, accounting for travel time, so you don’t lose any reservations, miss a movie, or arrive after the store closes.

The most important advice here is to do something intentional on Christmas, even if it's sleeping in, so the day doesn't feel depressing or empty. So hit the slopes, suck down some dim sum, or keep your couch from floating away, but be sure you make Christmas your own.

#3329. Aaron Rodgers Quits Steelers After Benching, Blasts Coach Mike McCarthy

12:03 PM PT -- The Steelers are officially releasing Aaron Rodgers

Aaron Rodgers says he's not returning to Pittsburgh after his shocking benching by the Steelers ... and he's unloading on Mike McCarthy, claiming the head coach has been sleeping through meetings, skipping team activities, and even forgetting which NFL team he's coaching.

The four-time MVP went off during Wednesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show" ... alleging McCarthy has been dozing off in meetings since training camp, missing walk-throughs and even breaking down a huddle by shouting "1, 2, 3, Packers" during Sunday's loss to the Eagles.

Rodgers -- who said he was given the day off -- says he's confronted McCarthy about his well-being numerous times, even suggesting he step aside and let someone else lead the team ... but claims the coach gets angry and denies anything is wrong.

And Rodgers says the bad blood runs deep ... claiming McCarthy still hasn't forgiven him for getting fired in Green Bay. He says the issues went on for 10 years with the Packers and could've remained private in Pittsburgh ... but he's breaking his silence over what he calls a lack of professionalism.

Rodgers also revealed he's asked the Steelers to release him ... after learning from teammate Pat Freiermuth that he'd been benched, despite meeting with McCarthy just hours earlier.

As was reported ... Pittsburgh announced late Tuesday that Mason Rudolph would start Friday against the Denver Broncos, with Rodgers inactive.

Rodgers insists he genuinely cares about McCarthy and even takes some responsibility for the mess ... admitting he vouched for his former coach to get the Steelers job in the first place.

#3328. AirPods 5 vs AirPods Pro 3: Which should you buy this holiday season?

The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts. If you’re shopping for AirPods, Apple sells three different models: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. Here’s how they compare.

AirPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

The case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:

The key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

If you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice …

AirPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. With that in-ear design, AirPods Pro 3 can offer up to 3x stronger noise cancellation than AirPods 5. In my testing, this difference is notable.

AirPods Pro 3 also offer several other features you won’t find on AirPods 5, including a heart rate sensor for workouts, plus Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features.

I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. I love the in-ear fit, and the ANC still impresses me, whether I’m at home or somewhere like a coffee shop.

If you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. This is especially true when AirPods Pro 3 are on sale, like they are right now at $149. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

Finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

This year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

AirPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

If you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.

Are you planning to buy anyone AirPods this holiday season? Are they on your wishlist? Let us know down in the comments.

#3327. Sam Rockwell’s New Spy Thriller Officially Says Goodbye to 1,000 Theaters

The last time Sam Rockwell worked with Martin McDonagh, he ended up winning an Academy Award for his performance in Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri, having previously worked with McDonagh on Seven Psychopaths. There were another nine Oscar nominations for McDonagh's work four years ago when he reunited Colin Farrell and Brendan Gleeson for The Banshees of Inisherin, and this year, it's the turn of Rockwell and John Malkovich to play two men whose relationship is explored through McDonagh's own distinctive brand of dark comedy. Unfortunately, if you've been planning to see the movie over Thanksgiving weekend, it's about to become considerably more difficult to find a theater showing it.

According to the latest theater count figures from The Numbers, McDonagh's Wild Horse Nine has officially lost 1,000 theaters heading into its fourth weekend of release, reducing its domestic theatrical footprint by exactly 50%. Having opened in 1,100 theaters on November 6, the movie expanded to 2,175 locations in its second weekend, but it will now be playing in 100 fewer theaters than it was on opening day.

Wild Horse Nine is alos nearing the $20 million milestone, having made $18.31 million domestically to date, with $2.46 million of that coming last weekend, when its grosses fell by 46%. The movie was averaging $1,231 per theater over the weekend, although that figure dropped to just $192 on Monday. With Thanksgiving bringing a particularly competitive weekend for theaters, McDonagh's movie has now lost more than 54% of its locations since the second weekend of its release.

McDonagh takes us to Chile in 1973, where two CIA agents are sent to Easter Island shortly before the military coup. For Malkovich's Chris, who's spending an increasing amount of time contemplating his own mortality, there's quite a bit of history between himself and Rockwell's Lee to reckon with, and things become rather more complicated for the two men when Chris befriends a pair of students on the island.

Written and directed by McDonagh, the movie features Malkovich (Con Air) as Chris Carlisle, Rockwell (Moon) as Lee Chesterfield, Steve Buscemi (Boardwalk Empire) as MJ, Mariana di Girolamo (Ema) as Monica, Ailín Salas (The German Doctor) as Alicia, Tom Waits (Seven Psychopaths) as Jim, and Parker Posey (The White Lotus) as Marge.

Wild Horse Nine is currently playing in theaters. Stay tuned to Collider for all the latest box office news and updates.

The BirdBuddy has been one of the most popular smart bird feeders since it hit the market a few years ago, but even with Black Friday discounts, the BirdBuddy Home is still a pricey $199. However, the company recently came out with a cheaper alternative: the BirdBuddy Nook starts at $169, but can be found for as little as $99 for Black Friday.

I’ve been testing out the BirdBuddy Nook for the last few weeks in my yard, and I think it’s a fine budget option for those who want to get into smart bird watching.

The BirdBuddy Nook Solar has a 2K HDR camera with a 135° wide-angle view that can be rotated horizontally or vertically. It has a capacity of 3.8 cups (0.9 L) of birdseed.

The larger of BirdBuddy's feeders, the Home can be filled with up to 6 cups / 1.4 liters of birdseed. It can be pole- or wall-mounted, and comes with a metal attachment to hang it from a branch.

The BirdBuddy Nook regularly costs $169 and $189 for the BirdBuddy Solar. For Black Friday, the base model has been discounted to $99, and the Solar model to $129. If you can afford the solar model, go for it — it’ll save you from having to recharge the camera module. I’ve been using the Solar model, and not once have I had to plug it in.

You can also find the older BirdBuddy Pro Solar for sale at Amazon for $179, but that camera is locked to a vertical orientation.

So what’s the difference between BirdBuddy’s feeders, other than the price? Mostly it comes down to capacity. The BirdBuddy Home ($299; on sale for $199) can fit more seed than the Nook, so you won’t have to fill it as often, unless you have ravenous squirrels in your yard, like I do.

Of course, to get the most out of either feeder, you need to sign up for a BirdBuddy subscription, which starts at $7.99/month or $69.99/year. That lets you record video at the highest quality, enjoy automatic AI recognition, and the ability to connect it to Alexa+.

The other major difference is in how you fill the feeder. The entire roof of the Nook hinges upwards so that you can fill its innards; the Home has a smaller opening in its rear. I found it’s very easy to accidentally overfill the Nook, especially if it’s mounted on a pole.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Otherwise, the Nook has the same camera as the BirdBuddy Home, which, while not as good as the now-discontinued BirdBuddy Pro, delivers more than respectable 2K videos and photos. Like the Home, the Nook’s camera can be rotated so you can record either portrait or landscape videos. I’m still not a fan of how the camera has a bit of lens distortion, so that objects near the edges are elongated.

Birdbuddy claims that the Nook’s smaller shelf is better at deterring squirrels. I initially set it up with the perch extender, which may have been a mistake, as it gave the little furry creatures an easy spot to clean out the feeder. Don't get this attachment if you have problems with squirrels.

Given that the cameras on the BirdBuddy Home and BirdBuddy Nook are identical, I would definitely opt for the cheaper Nook; yes, you’ll have to refill it more often, but it’s $110 less expensive. During Black Friday, the price difference is just $70, but that’s still pretty significant.

As I mentioned earlier, get the model with the built-in solar panel. It’ll save you the hassle of having to schlep out to your yard in the middle of winter just to see the squirrels raiding your supply.

I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did.

The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip update, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.

I’m happy to report that the new S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

Everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri was sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.

The new Health Sensing System makes Apple Watch Series 12 better at tracking key metrics like heart rate and steps. But this isn’t a case where accuracy is the only improvement.

Because of the new health sensors, Series 12 offers three complications not available before:

The complications let you see up-to-date readings on your current heart rate, step count, and readiness score right from your watch face. These are very welcome additions that meaningfully improve the Apple Watch’s health and wellness feature set.

I’ve been using the watchOS 27.3 beta, which adds a new Siri Recap feature for Series 12 models that I really love.

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment.

Most of what Siri documents, I’ll never need to reference and it gets deleted automatically. But for those times I have trouble remembering a key piece of information, I’ve found Siri Recap a very convenient addition.

Apple Watch Series 12 offers largely the same battery life as Series 11, though it will last 25% longer for outdoor workouts.

More battery is always nice, but I’m especially a fan of the faster charging available on Series 12. Here’s how it stacks up to Series 11:

I wear my Apple Watch to bed and generally try to top it off quickly in the evening, but I’m not always great at giving it much time on the charger. With faster charging support on Series 12, my poor planning isn’t a problem.

#3320. 10 Hidden Controls Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

You can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely new side of the game.

If you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

Hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

If you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

When you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

While driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

Stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

When you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.
